title: Influential-coordinate approximation
statement: Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $\tau>0$. There exists $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ depending only on $J_\tau(f)=\{i:I_i(f)\ge\tau\}$ such that $\mathbb E(f^{\le k}-g)^2\le n\tau$. For a real cube function $h$, define $I_i(h)=\tfrac14\mathbb E_x(h(x)-h(x^{(i)}))^2$, where $x^{(i)}$ flips coordinate $i$ and $\mathbb E_x$ is uniform expectation.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity n
k is a natural number (truncation level)
replaced:
For every $f$, every level $k$ and every $\tau > 0$ there is a function $g$ that is a
junta on the $\tau$-influential coordinates $J_\tau(f)$ and satisfies
$\E\big[(f_{\le k} - g)^2\big] \le n\tau$.
